gloss: ignoring what one hears; letting something pass without responding

definitions.gloss: ignoring what one hears; letting something pass without responding
definitions.explanation: The act of hearing something but choosing not to respond to it or act on it. Most commonly appears in the negative pattern 聞き捨てならない, meaning something one cannot ignore.

examples.japanese: その{発言|はつげん}は{聞|き}き{捨|す}てならない。
{聞|き}き{捨|す}てならないことを{言|い}われて、{反論|はんろん}した。
examples.english: I was told something I couldn't let pass, so I argued back.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}の{悪口|わるくち}を{聞|き}き{捨|す}てにできず、「それは{違|ちが}う」と{口|くち}を{挟|はさ}んだ。
examples.english: Unable to let the badmouthing of my friend pass, I interjected, "That's not true."

notes:
Compound of {聞|き}き (hearing) + {捨|す}て (discarding). Almost always used in the negative.

KEY PATTERNS:
- {聞|き}き{捨|す}てならない (cannot be ignored; something outrageous)
- {聞|き}き{捨|す}てにできない (cannot let pass)
- {聞|き}き{捨|す}てにする (to let pass without comment — rare, literary)

USAGE NOTE:
The phrase {聞|き}き{捨|す}てならない expresses indignation — the speaker feels compelled to respond because what they heard was offensive, unfair, or outrageous. It is a moderately formal expression used in both speech and writing.
